requirement: A GitHub Actions CI workflow MUST run, for pull requests and pushes to `main`, these checks: `cargo habeas coverage -- --locked --workspace` under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.run`, `cargo test --locked --doc --workspace`, `mdbook test`, the autofix controller tests with `node --test .github/scripts/autofix.test.mjs`, and, in a separate job, the Symposium session-start hook smoke test `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py`. It MUST also build the book with the combined coverage reports of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`, including the coverage collected by these checks, and on a push to `main`, only after every check job passes, it MUST deploy the generated `book/` directory to GitHub Pages. The book MUST set `output.html.site-url` to `/habeas-codicem/` for project-site hosting.
rationale:
The single marked test, `tests/repository.rs#fn[ci_tests_pull_requests_and_main_then_deploys_the_book_from_main]`, checks every obligation in `requirements.integration.ci`. I compared it with `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which holds the `{impl}` markers for the requirement.

- **Triggers:** the test asserts the exact `on:` block, which has `push` with `branches: [main]` plus `pull_request`. This covers "for pull requests and pushes to `main`".
- **Required checks in `test-and-build`:** the test finds each of these commands in the job text:
  - `node --test .github/scripts/autofix.test.mjs`
  - `cargo habeas coverage -- --locked --workspace`
  - `cargo test --locked --doc --workspace`
  - `mdbook test`
- **Coverage gate:** `cargo habeas coverage-check` isn't in the requirement text. The test still asserts that this step has no `if` and no `continue-on-error`, so a coverage failure fails the job. The `requirements.test-coverage.run` text is cited here only as context.
- **Symposium smoke test in a separate job:** the test reads the `symposium-hook` job and asserts it runs `python3 tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py`. Separation holds because the step sits in its own job.
- **Book built with combined coverage, including coverage from these checks:** the test asserts the order of the steps. The node tests, release build, coverage run, coverage check, doc tests, `mdbook test` and `mdbook build` must appear in that order, and the Pages artifact upload comes after them. It also asserts the upload `path: book`. So the book is built after the coverage run and the other checks, and `book/` is what gets uploaded.
- **Deploy only after every check job passes, and only on a push to `main`:** the test reads the `deploy` job and asserts the `if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` condition. It also asserts `needs: [test-and-build, symposium-hook]`, which covers both check jobs, and `actions/deploy-pages@v4`.
- **Site URL:** the test parses `book.toml` and asserts that `output.html.site-url` equals `/habeas-codicem/`.

The test is string- and ordering-based, so it would accept `continue-on-error` or `if` added to a check step other than the coverage gate. The requirement doesn't name that failure mode. The coverage-collection wording is also loose, since the doctest and `mdbook test` steps don't visibly collect coverage. The test does pin the ordering and the `mdbook build` step that consumes the coverage, which is the testable part. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} ci

A GitHub Actions CI workflow MUST run, for pull requests and pushes to `main`, these checks: `cargo habeas coverage -- --locked --workspace` under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.run`, `cargo test --locked --doc --workspace`, `mdbook test`, the autofix controller tests with `node --test .github/scripts/autofix.test.mjs`, and, in a separate job, the Symposium session-start hook smoke test `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py`. It MUST also build the book with the combined coverage reports of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`, including the coverage collected by these checks, and on a push to `main`, only after every check job passes, it MUST deploy the generated `book/` directory to GitHub Pages. The book MUST set `output.html.site-url` to `/habeas-codicem/` for project-site hosting.
:::{req} run
`habeas coverage [-- <nextest arguments>]` MUST run LLVM-instrumented Rust tests
through `cargo nextest run`, forwarding the supplied arguments and preserving
nextest's configured test concurrency, filtering, and retries. With no supplied
arguments it MUST select the workspace.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST show the number of
selected test attempts and summarize coverage excluded because it is stale,
unavailable, or from a historical build configuration. Detailed test identities,
run provenance, and per-test execution data MUST remain in the saved coverage
artifacts rather than being included in the generated book.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST visibly identify incomplete coverage and MUST NOT imply that every current
test has coverage merely because all available records are valid.
